thread:
alex: Heads up — ap-south1 is seeing a spike in GPU attach failures starting ~09:12 UTC. Root cause looks tied to local NVMe flapping during large KV-cache spills :frowning:
ops-bot: ALERT: node=gnode-apse1-433 nvme_io_errors=127 scrub_queue_depth=74
maya: digging in — large model loads triggered huge kvcache spills -> tinywrites avalanche and metadata storm
lee: that pattern sounds familiar but amplitude is higher than prior incidents
maya: paste from node logs:
```
2026-03-23T09:12:03Z kvcache: spill-start size=18.4GB keys=1.2M
2026-03-23T09:12:03Z nvme: submit_bio: len=4KB qdepth=128 ret=EIO
2026-03-23T09:12:05Z scrub: enqueue 1200 async metadata writes
2026-03-23T09:12:06Z attach: attempt_id=tx-448 fail=nvme_io_error
```
sam: urgent: workload backlog ~120 GPU-hours, retries are increasing cost. Need immediate mitigation
maya: short-term mitigations: throttle kvcache spill concurrency, reduce janitor parallelism, and pause large model rollout in ap-south1
alex: can we toggle janitor to only run one scrub at a time in that region?
lee: ops config flip: `janitor.max_parallel_scrubs = 1` and lower `kvcache.spill_batch_size = 64MB` should help
nirav: I'll deploy a canary (5% of ap-south1) with those settings and watch attach success. If I/O contention drops we should see attach success go up from ~62% to ~90% per our estimate
sam: timeline? coordinating with capacity-planning — the backlog is hitting delayed SLAs
maya: ops-bot: create incident and tag @capacity-team
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-23-apse1-nvme-spill (link)
lee: also pulling SMART/firmware counters — may be controller PM toggles aligning with spill start causing extra retries
alex: who owns firmware correlation?
lee: I'll run a SMART sweep and diff against baseline thermal logs for the node group
nirav: canary deploy started at 09:14:12 UTC to 8 nodes, monitoring iostat and attach histogram
ops-bot: deploy event: nirav applied `janitor-throttle-apse1` to canary pool at 2026-03-23T09:14:12Z
maya: short-term telemetry: canary nodes iops down ~35%, attach success increased to 84% :thumbsup:
sam: sounds promising, should we expand to 50%? what's the risk of slowing scrubs (reclaim backlog, potential increased S3 repair traffic)?
lee: tradeoffs: slower scrubs -> more ephemeral space used and delayed reclamation, which can trigger cross-region replica rebuilds and S3 egress. Need infra lead signoff for a fleet rollout beyond canary
alex: @infra-leads please weigh in on the tradeoff — we need capacity freed without inflating cross-region costs
nirav: monitoring SMART for re-write amplification; scheduling periodic collects: `collect-smart --nodes=canary --every=30s --out=/tmp/smart-apse1-canary.log`
sre-bot: scheduled job created: collect-smart (canary) every 30s
maya: I'll draft the incident postmortem checklist: observed metrics, mitigation, cost impact estimate, followups (firmware, model-load concurrency limits, pre-warm prefixes)
sam: also notifying capacity-planning: backlog ~120 GPU-hours, suggest requeue low-priority jobs to other regions if multiplicative failure continues
lee: I'm running a deeper firmware/driver correlation now — if controller power-save toggles coincide with high qdepth we may need firmware update or driver knob
alex: OK — action items: sam coordinate infra leads and capacity team, nirav expand canary to 50% after 10m stable, lee finish SMART/firmware dive, maya own postmortem draft
ops-bot: INC-2026-03-23-apse1-nvme-spill updated with assignees and checklist
maya: adding quick note: long-term fixes: limit model-load concurrency per node, spill backpressure in runtime, and pre-warm key prefixes during deployments to avoid huge single spills
nirav: rolling expansion to 50% in 8 minutes if canary stays green
lee: collecting SMART diffs now. early look: write-amplification counters spike coincident with spill-start events
sam: cost note for leads: temporary scrub throttling saves immediate attach failures but may increase background repair S3 egress and retention costs — will quantify in postmortem
alex: reconvene in 20m to decide fleet-wide rollout. Ping this thread with any regressions immediately
